title: Joe's health, build, and feeding the band
summary: Joe died at 54, was heavy as a boy, and Stella fed bands such as Lee Collins, Dutrey and Ory with beans and rice.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Yeah, that's right, that's right, that's right. I had a lot of fun with those two boys. I had a lot of fun with all of the boys. All of the boys. Every one of them. And I liked them all. But, as I say, Joe was only 54 when he died. He wasn't really old at all. No! He should've, I thought he should've at least lived until he was 65, 70. Yes, he should've lived. Because a man that doesn't drink, and it didn't dissipate as I say. He didn't dissipate.
Was he always pretty heavy when he was a boy? Always, always. Sort of. Always.

Always. Because he always ate cornbread and he had salad food and very few things he didn't like. And he drank plenty of water. Plenty of water. Plenty of water all the time. He had water kept him fat.
Yes, because of the starches, I guess. Yes. Lee Collins told me too, when he went to Chicago, you had a big meal for him the first night you got there.

Oh, yes. Oh, yes. I always, I was always nice with the boys. Because I wanted to always remember me as Joe's wife. And Joe was so nice to me. He was so nice to me. So good to me and my people. So I had to try to make him happy. And the only way to do it was to treat his friends nice.

That was the only way I know. I couldn't repay him in any other way. I had to be nice. And all I could do was just cook a big pot of beans and tell them all come over. And that's all they wanted. Beans and rice. And Lee Collins and Dutre and Ori and the whole gang of mine have them sometimes. And Joe liked company too. He liked company. He was very fond of company. And he liked for them to eat. But as I said, he wasn't a drinking man. He wasn't a drinking man at all. But he had, he had a hard time with it. He had a bad time.
